cli_intro: Run MetaDash without opening the window: sync, write reports and exports, check status. Useful for scheduled reports (cron, launchd, Task Scheduler). The command line can run while the app is open; only one sync runs at a time.
cli_installed_at: The metadash command is installed at
cli_not_installed: The metadash command is not installed. You can still run the app binary with --cli (below).
cli_not_on_path: This folder is not on your PATH yet. Add it to your shell profile (e.g. export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH") or call the file with its full path.
cli_not_on_path_win: Add this folder to your user PATH (Settings → System → About → Advanced system settings → Environment Variables), then open a new terminal.
cli_install_hint_mac: Installs a small script into /usr/local/bin (or ~/.local/bin when that folder is not writable) that starts MetaDash with --cli.
cli_install_hint_win: Installs metadash.cmd into %LOCALAPPDATA%\MetaDash\bin; add that folder to PATH.
cli_install_hint_linux: Installs a small script into ~/.local/bin that starts MetaDash with --cli.
cli_without_install_hint: The app binary itself is the command-line tool when started with --cli. Default install locations:
cli_ex_status: Last sync, connection health and quota
cli_ex_report: Last month's PDF report, one file per account of a client
cli_ex_export: Accounts and posts as an Excel workbook
cli_json_hint: Add --json for machine-readable output and --help after any command for its options.
cli_schedule_hint: Scheduling examples (cron, launchd, Task Scheduler) and headless Linux notes are in docs/cli.md.
cli_windows_output_hint: On Windows the app may not print to the console; use --out for files and --log-file for the messages.
cli_exit_codes: Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 error · 2 wrong arguments · 3 partly failed · 4 reconnect needed · 5 a sync is already running · 6 read-only workspace.
